title: Book Three · Chapter 87: Twenty Each
story:
On Sunday, Leo comes to the green door after nine.

Ronan has three ordinary books on the table. One has animal stories in a green cover. One is a thin yellow puzzle book. The third has simple outdoor games.

The first two books were gifts from Mum years ago. He bought the games book with his own pocket money. All three belong to him.

His birthday book stays on the shelf. He checked the photo inside it this morning, then closed the cover.

Leo lays three books beside Ronan's. Railway stories, riddles, and a thin book about gardens.

“These three,” he says.

They open them and check the names inside. None came from a library. Leo keeps his favourite story at his grandmother's.

Ronan takes out his money envelope. There are thirty yuan in it now. Some are coins; some are folded notes.

He puts ten yuan back for his own spending. The other twenty go in the middle of the table.

Leo takes a different envelope from his bag.

“Twenty for the books,” he says. “My ten for the visit stays here.”

He puts the separate ten back in his own pocket.

Ronan writes twenty beside his name and twenty beside Leo's. The shared cash is forty yuan. They put it in Leo's empty envelope.

“Half each,” Leo says.

“The work and the money?”

“Yes. We each put in three books too.”

They agree that the six books will join the shared stock. Any money from them will stay with the book money. They will share the final money and remaining books equally when the sale is finished.

For now, neither takes shared money for his own spending.

Mum comes to the table with her tea. She looks at the two names and the little pile of cash.

“Your own?”

“Ours,” Ronan says. “Twenty each.”

She nods and takes her work to the window.

Leo lifts the game book.

“You may want this back when we lose a game.”

“We have a ball now.”

“Then we can lose outdoors.”

Ronan laughs. He puts the six books together and counts them again.

They need more stories, but they also need bags and a table. Forty yuan has to cover those things too.

Leo wants to go to the book stall now. Ronan takes one clean sheet for the purchases.

At the door, Ronan leaves his personal ten yuan in his own envelope on the shelf.

The shared cash goes with the purchase sheet. Ronan puts all six books in a dry place on the shelf. Then the boys leave for the stall.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

shared cash＝共同使用的现金；stock＝待售库存；purchase＝购买；equally＝平均地。

## 理解问题

1. 两人各拿多少个人钱投入？共同现金有多少，个人零花钱有没有混进来？
2. 六本自有旧书怎样加入售卖？他们打算什么时候分剩下的钱和书？

## 读句子

**The shared cash is forty yuan.**

拆开看：The shared cash / is / forty yuan.

共同现金／是／四十元。
